purpose: Add France/New Caledonia as a mechanism-control case to the existing protest/network comparison and reduce false attribution by distinguishing DNS blocking from DPI/TLS/RST interference.
new_france_contribution: Mainland France 2023 demonstrates severe unrest without a confirmed Internet shutdown.
New Caledonia 2024 demonstrates state-ordered protest-era selective platform blocking through a documented, comparatively simple DNS mechanism on Mobilis/OPT-NC.
The case proves that political timing plus platform unreachability is insufficient to infer DPI, TSPU, PROTEI or foreign control.
The later Conseil d'Etat ruling provides a legal-accountability layer absent from several other comparison cases.
PROTEI client-list entry 'Orange BS' remains a lead only and is not counted as French public-network deployment evidence.
updated_spider_rule: A protest-correlated service failure gets no vendor/control-plane attribution weight until the mechanism is identified. DNS manipulation, TCP RST injection, TLS timeout, BGP/routing withdrawal, radio interference and physical power loss are separate evidence classes.
reason: France adds a powerful false-positive control but does not supply the missing current cross-border path-specific or vendor-control-channel bridge.
